title: Lesson 28: The One-Page Cheat Sheet: The Essentials on a Single Sheet
description: Turning twenty-seven lessons into one glanceable reference: why the one-page limit carries the value, how a cue differs from a lesson, and the five blocks every work cheat sheet needs.

questions.question: Per the lesson "The One-Page Cheat Sheet: The Essentials on a Single Sheet", why does the one-page limit matter?
options: It forces you to keep only the essentials, and it makes the sheet something you can see at once rather than page through
It matches the standard printed page size
It keeps the sheet cheap to print
It limits how many words each line may hold
questions.explanation: The lesson says the limit is not a style preference but the constraint that forces the essentials, because a sheet that grows to two or three pages becomes something you read again.

questions.question: What does the lesson say a cheat sheet is, as opposed to a lesson?
options: A condensed version of the lessons you can read to learn the skills cold
A cue that reminds you of a skill you already know, so you do not forget to apply it when the pressure is on
A collection of long worked examples
questions.explanation: The lesson says each line exists to remind you of a skill you already know, and if a line needs a paragraph of explanation to be understood, it does not belong on the sheet.

questions.question: Which shorthand does the lesson give for the brief?
questions.explanation: The lesson calls the brief the single most used product of the series and reduces it to the four-word shorthand of Role, Task, Context, and Format.
